# The vocabulary of TinyC, exported from the compiler that defines it.
#
# Generated by `cargo run --bin export-vocabulary` — do not edit. What this is
# a copy *of* lives in `src/vocabulary.rs` and `src/ast.rs`; what it is a
# copy *for* is `ide/intellij`, whose token table is generated from it.
#
#   role     <name>    word | symbol
#   token    <name>    <spelling>              <role>
#   valued   <name>    <what a diagnostic calls it>
#   builtin  <name>    <parameters, by comma>  <return type>
#   spec     <letter>  <what it writes>

format	1

# What a token is for. A `word` is a name no program may take; a
# `symbol` is punctuation. Whoever reads this makes a set per role
# rather than knowing the roles, so a new one needs nothing said.
role	type	word
role	control	word
role	construct	word
role	literal	word
role	punctuation	symbol
role	operator	symbol

# Every token spelled exactly one way.
token	INT_KW	int	type
token	STRING_KW	string	type
token	CHAR_KW	char	type
token	BOOL_KW	bool	type
token	IF_KW	if	control
token	ELSE_KW	else	control
token	WHILE_KW	while	control
token	FOR_KW	for	control
token	FN_KW	fn	control
token	RETURN_KW	return	control
token	BREAK_KW	break	control
token	CONTINUE_KW	continue	control
token	ENUM_KW	enum	control
token	MATCH_KW	match	control
token	CLASS_KW	class	control
token	PRINT_KW	print	construct
token	PRINTLN_KW	println	construct
token	LEN_KW	len	construct
token	PUSH_KW	push	construct
token	TRUE_KW	true	literal
token	FALSE_KW	false	literal
token	LPAREN	(	punctuation
token	RPAREN	)	punctuation
token	LBRACE	{	punctuation
token	RBRACE	}	punctuation
token	LBRACKET	[	punctuation
token	RBRACKET	]	punctuation
token	SEMI	;	punctuation
token	COMMA	,	punctuation
token	DOT	.	punctuation
token	COLON	:	punctuation
token	COLON_COLON	::	punctuation
token	ARROW	->	operator
token	FAT_ARROW	=>	operator
token	EQ	=	operator
token	PLUS	+	operator
token	MINUS	-	operator
token	STAR	*	operator
token	SLASH	/	operator
token	PERCENT	%	operator
token	BANG	!	operator
token	EQ_EQ	==	operator
token	BANG_EQ	!=	operator
token	LT	<	operator
token	LE	<=	operator
token	GT	>	operator
token	GE	>=	operator
token	AND_AND	&&	operator
token	OR_OR	||	operator

# The tokens that carry a value, and so are spelled every way rather
# than one. An editor still needs to tell them apart to colour them.
valued	INT_LITERAL	integer literal
valued	STRING_LITERAL	string literal
valued	CHAR_LITERAL	character literal
valued	IDENTIFIER	identifier

# Names already in the signature table when the first line is checked.
builtin	read_line		string
builtin	eof		bool
builtin	is_int	string	bool

# What a `%` in a format string may be followed by.
spec	d	an int
spec	c	a char
spec	s	a string
spec	b	a bool
spec	e	a variant of an enum
